title: Benefit vs Advantage Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: A six-card sorting quiz in which learners classify value-proposition statements from a mobile dog-grooming idea as customer Benefits (why the customer wants it) or founder Advantages (why this founder can deliver it), with immediate green or amber feedback and a one-sentence explanation for each card.

educational.topic: Customer benefit versus founder advantage in a value proposition
learningObjectives: Classify value-proposition statements as a customer Benefit (why the customer wants it) or a founder Advantage (why this founder can deliver it) by applying the chapter's definitions

controls.label: Benefit
controls.purpose: Classify the current statement as a customer benefit

controls.label: Advantage
controls.purpose: Classify the current statement as a founder advantage

controls.label: Try Again
controls.purpose: Reshuffle the cards and start over

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification quiz with immediate corrective feedback
keyQuestions: Is this sentence about an outcome in the customer's life, or about the founder's background?
Why is 'affordable, convenient grooming' a benefit even though it sounds like a pitch?
commonMisconceptions: Any sentence that sounds like a sales pitch must be a founder advantage
A founder circumstance that helps the customer is a benefit rather than an advantage
assessmentOpportunities: Score at least 5 of 6 on a second, shuffled attempt
Write one benefit and one advantage sentence for your own idea and have a partner label them
